headline: Algorithmic and indexing advances cut runtime and memory across sequence analysis tasks
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Algorithms
summary: Eight November 2026 preprints report speed and memory gains for mapping, RNA structure, single-cell, indexing and pangenome tasks, alongside a mapper memory characterization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is efficiency engineering for sequence-derived computation, with accuracy and resource use reported together. ScanFold3 reports 38-129x gains over ScanFold2, and LinearRaccess computes RNA accessibility in O(N) time without base-pair span limits. brisc and the extended simpleaf target multithreaded and memory-frugal single-cell analysis, with brisc running a 10M-cell workflow in 3 minutes. Hybrid RY-mers in strobealign improve aDNA alignment and run 4-6x faster than BWA-aln. Zindex offers compact colored sequence indexing, and hub labeling enables exact distance queries on large human pangenome graphs. The arXiv characterization of read mappers adds systems-level evidence, identifying memory-bound functions. The problems are distinct, so the commonality is methodological: replacing costly dense or approximate computation with structured data representations or pruning.
